key_insight: A coupled pore-scale lattice Boltzmann model shows how thermal perturbations can drive salinity changes and non-uniform freezing in sea-ice brine channels.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports detailed simulation of heat transfer, solute redistribution, and evolving pore geometry in phase-changing porous materials.
method: Couple liquid solute transport with conjugate solid–liquid heat transfer.
Track direction-dependent interface motion using a link-based Volume-of-Pixel formulation.
Treat solute redistribution at moving interfaces with a generalized Robin boundary condition.
evidence_signal: Thermal benchmarks validate phase change, literature tests show first- to second-order convergence for the Robin treatment, and diffusive brine-channel simulations recover ideal mushy-layer behaviour under appropriate scale separation.
watch_item: The sea-ice application is local and purely diffusive; performance with advective transport or larger-scale channel networks is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: A coupled lattice Boltzmann model for pore-scale mushy-layer dynamics with application to sea ice
